frontmatter.title: The Nyawice puts a leaf-spring F1 mount under a friction-fit-cat-ears Alice
frontmatter.lede: An Alice-layout board with a leaf-spring F1 mount, a 9-degree typing angle, and four colorways of friction-fit silicone cat ears ran at CannonKeys through 2026-05-17. The mount type is the editorial story; the cat ears are the conversation.
frontmatter.author: thock

frontmatter.title: How Topre's electrocapacitive switches actually work
frontmatter.lede: Topre is not just another switch — it is a third sensing lineage, parallel to the MX-style contact switches and the Hall-effect newcomers. Understanding why HHKB and Realforce typists pay what they pay starts with the fact that a Topre keypress does not close a circuit at all.
frontmatter.author: thock

frontmatter.title: ZMK is becoming the wireless default for premium prebuilts
frontmatter.lede: A five-board flagship lineup running ZMK isn't a niche move; it's a market signal that an open-source firmware that lived in DIY-wireless territory for half a decade has crossed into mainstream-prebuilt anchor status. The vendor side has finally caught up with where the cohort already was.
frontmatter.author: thock

frontmatter.title: How Hall-effect switches actually sense a keypress
frontmatter.lede: A Hall-effect switch is not a faster MX switch. It is a different sensing lineage — a magnet in the stem, a sensor on the PCB, and an analog voltage where contact closure used to be. The features the marketing pages lead with all unwind from that one architectural fact.
frontmatter.author: thock

frontmatter.title: Switch films: do they actually do anything?
frontmatter.lede: Thin POM shims between your switch housings cost five dollars and promise a tighter, better-sounding switch. The mechanism is real. Whether it matters on your specific switches is a separate question.

vendors.name: CannonKeys
vendors.description: Boutique keyboard vendor based in the United States. Stocks switches, keycaps, and runs in-house and partnered group buys for boards and accessories.

vendors.name: Delta Key Co.
vendors.description: French mechanical keyboard vendor founded by two brothers. Sells keyboards, keycaps, switches, and accessories; ships from Grimaud, France.

vendors.name: Divinikey
vendors.description: US-based mechanical keyboard retailer headquartered in Los Angeles, California, stocking keyboards, keycap sets, switches, and accessories; runs group buys for custom keyboard projects including DCS and GMK keycap sets.

vendors.name: Drop
vendors.description: US storefront and platform for community-driven keyboard, audio, and gaming products. Co-develops MT3 keycap profiles with Matt3o and runs in-house Drop-branded switches and boards.

vendors.name: KBDfans
vendors.description: China-based mechanical keyboard vendor with a long-running storefront for boards, switches, keycaps, and accessories; hosts a large slate of GMK and in-house group buys with multi-region proxies.

vendors.name: Keychron
vendors.description: Popular keyboard brand based in Hong Kong known for the Q line (gasket-mounted aluminum prebuilts with QMK/VIA support), the K line (wireless mechanical for everyday use), and the Q Ultra series featuring ZMK firmware and magnetic Hall-effect switches. One of the highest-volume vendors in the enthusiast-adjacent prebuilt market, stocked widely across Amazon and direct.

vendors.name: NovelKeys
vendors.description: Morgantown, West Virginia-based vendor that runs in-house switches (Cream, Silk) and partners on group buys for keycaps and boards. One of the most-cited NA storefronts for enthusiast switch SKUs.

vendors.name: Prototypist
vendors.description: UK-based mechanical keyboard vendor handling regional fulfillment and customs for GMK and DCS keycap-set group buys hosted by other studios, alongside its own in-house kit and colorway group buys.

vendors.name: Qwertykeys
vendors.description: China-based custom mechanical keyboard manufacturer and direct-to-consumer storefront, based in Guangdong. Best known for the QK65/QK75/QK80/QK100 board line; ships direct with wireless and hot-swap PCB options as standard configurator choices rather than group-buy upsell tiers.

vendors.name: Wooting
vendors.description: Dutch maker of Hall-effect keyboards and the originator of rapid-trigger for PC gaming. The Wooting 60HE and Wooting 60HE+ are the benchmarks the rest of the analog-input category measures against: per-key actuation depth, analog axis output to games, and the most mature rapid-trigger firmware stack in the segment. Wooting's software has a multi-year head start on configurator depth that newer HE entrants are actively closing.

vendors.name: Wuque Studio
vendors.description: China-based design studio and vendor known for in-house boards (Mammoth, Ikki68, Promise) and partnered group buys, sold direct from shop.wuquestudio.com with regional proxies.
